        return 0.0
    close = next((c for c in '})]' if c in closes), None)
    age = 0
    if close is not None:
        pending = stacks[OPEN_FOR[close]]
        count = token.count(close)
        age = position - pending[-count] if len(pending) >= count else 10000

    curly = close == '}'
    text = before.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t').replace('\\r', '\r')
    spaced = bool(text) and text[-1].isspace()
    line = text.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    blank_line = not line.strip()
    newlines = token.count('\n')

                return -0.055 if close == ')' else 0.023
            return 0.193 if curly else 0.031
        if curly:

        return 0.365 if newlines else 0.004

        return -0.406 if blank_line else 1.038
    if newlines >= 2:
        return 1.082
    return 1.434 if blank_line else 1.696

    position = prefix.position
    value = closing_strength(token, before, stacks, position)

    for char in token:

"""Closing brackets that end a long span.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:6132 fires on a closing bracket (`}`, `)`, `]`) when
the bracket it closes was opened well back in the text, i.e. the block it ends is
long. A `}` that closes a block opened a few tokens earlier stays near zero; one that
closes a block opened 30+ tokens earlier fires near its maximum. A `)` or `]` needs a
longer gap (roughly 10 to 60 tokens) before it fires. A closer whose opener is not in
the visible window (the row starts inside the block) also fires strongly.

Two smaller effects: the first token of each document is pushed slightly negative,
and everything else is near zero.

The program keeps a stack of open brackets per document, reset at each document
boundary (and at the row start), so it reads only the tokens up to the current one.
"""

READS = ()

CLOSER_OF = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
CLOSERS = set(")]}")

BRACE_SCALE, BRACE_FULL = 1.25, 30  # '}' reaches BRACE_SCALE once its opener is 30 tokens back
PAREN_SCALE, PAREN_START, PAREN_FULL = 1.3, 10, 60  # ')' and ']' ramp from 10 to 60 tokens
UNMATCHED = 1.2  # a closer whose opener is not in the window
DOC_START = -0.4  # first token of a document


def _ramp(x, lo, hi):
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (x - lo) / (hi - lo)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        start, stack = t, []  # new document (or row start): nothing open yet
    else:
        _, start, stack = carry
        stack = list(stack)

    value = DOC_START if t == start else 0.0
    first_closer = True
    for ch in token:
        if ch in CLOSER_OF:
            stack.append((CLOSER_OF[ch], t))
        elif ch in CLOSERS:
            opened = stack.pop()[1] if stack else None
            if first_closer:
                first_closer = False
                if opened is None:
                    value = UNMATCHED
                elif ch == "}":
                    value = BRACE_SCALE * _ramp(t - opened, 0, BRACE_FULL)
                else:
                    value = PAREN_SCALE * _ramp(t - opened, PAREN_START, PAREN_FULL)
    return (doc, start, stack), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 6133: a small, mostly-quiet detector.

Most of the time this component sits near zero. It has three things it does respond to:

1. Start of a document (the first token of a packed row, or the first token after a
   document boundary). The model resets attention there, so the activation depends only on
   the token itself. Ordinary tokens sit around -0.33; the chat marker <|im_start|> sits at +0.28.
2. A replacement character (U+FFFD, shown as "�") that completes a multi-byte character split
   across tokens. The strongest case is the long s "ſ" (UTF-8 C5 BF), whose second byte arrives
   as its own token; that gives about +2.6. Other completed Hangul syllables give a weak +0.3,
   and other completed characters a small +0.1. A replacement character that does not complete
   a character gives 0.
3. The email-obfuscation placeholder "[email protected]": the token " protected" right after
   "email" gives about +4.2.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The unexplained remainder is small, diffuse, token-level
noise (std about 0.05), which no short concept captures.
"""

READS = ()
RC = "�"  # replacement character: how a lone, incomplete UTF-8 byte decodes


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    pos = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    # 1. Document start: first token of the row, or first token after a document boundary.
    if pos == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.28 if token == "<|im_start|>" else -0.33

    # 3. Email-obfuscation placeholder "[email" + " protected".
    if token == " protected" and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "email":

    if token == RC:

                return None, 2.6
            if unicodedata.name(ch, "").startswith("HANGUL"):
                return None, 0.3
            return None, 0.1

    return None, 0.0

This does not attempt to explain non-English text or formula operators.

    r'^(?:dihydroxy|hydroxy|hydro|deoxy|di|tri|tetra|poly|organo|mono|'
    r'iso|allo|cyclo|chloro|bromo|fluoro|nitro|amino|de|oxy)'

    r'(?:enol|anol|thiol|thione|amide|amine|azole|cillin|mycin|cycline|'

    r'(?:acet|ethyl|methyl|benz|chlor|fluor|brom|iod|hydrox|sulf|sulph|'
    r'phosph|nitr|amino|carbox|gluc|glyc|sucro|lacto|fruct|fibr|kerat|'
    r'collag|(?:meth|eth|prop|but|pent|hex|hept|oct|non|dec)(?:an|en|yn))'

# newest token consists of that ending alone. Order resolves overlaps.

    'ine': (0.224, 0.396),
    'in': (0.0, 0.178),
    'ide': (-0.118, 0.655),
    'ate': (0.0, 0.219),
    'ite': (0.0, 0.076),
    'ane': (0.099, 0.402),
    'ene': (0.552, -0.073),
    'yne': (0.184, 0.0),
    'ose': (-0.051, 1.031),
    'ol': (0.0, 0.061),

    'ogen': (0.487, -0.278),
    'ic': (0.0, 0.0),
    'gen': (0.0, -0.107),

    'amino acid': 1.817,
    'carbohydrate': 0.432,
    'drug': -0.064,
    'acid': 0.28,
    'alcohol': -0.057,
    'subatomic particle': 0.048,

    found = list(COMMAND.finditer(text))

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:6140: a "long word" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Fires on English-style word tokens (letters only, optionally with a leading space, or a
  leading "." "_" "/" "-" as in code identifiers and paths), in proportion to their length
  in letters: about 0 for words of 4 letters or fewer ("the", "of", "is"), about 0.15 at 5
  letters, about 1.0 at 8, and capped at 1.8 from 10 letters up. The strongest tokens are
  long formal or technical vocabulary ("administrative", "implementation", "requirements",
  "workspace", "_modules").
- Fires on multi-character CJK tokens in proportion to their length: 0 for one character,
  about 0.5 for two, about 1.2 for three, capped at 1.8.
- Fires at 1.5 on long runs of indentation whitespace (9 or more characters, as in deeply
  nested code).
- Is negative, about -1, on the first token of each document (the model resets there).
- Everything else (punctuation, digits, short words) is 0.

Why: the activation is close to a function of which token it is, and for ordinary words the
main thing that separates high from low is how long the word is.
"""

import re

READS = ()

WORD = re.compile(r" ?[._/-]?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z_]*")
CJK = re.compile(r"[぀-ヿ㐀-鿿가-힯豈-﫿]+")
LETTERS_AT_ZERO = 4.5  # words up to about this many letters give 0
SLOPE = 0.3            # added per letter beyond that
CJK_AT_ZERO = 1.5      # CJK tokens up to about this many characters give 0
CJK_SLOPE = 0.5
CAP = 1.8              # the largest value of a word or CJK token
INDENT_MIN = 9         # whitespace runs at least this long
INDENT_VALUE = 1.5
DOC_START_VALUE = -1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    documents = prefix.document_ids
    if len(documents) == 1 or documents[-2] != documents[-1]:
        return None, DOC_START_VALUE
    if token.strip() == "":
        return None, INDENT_VALUE if len(token) >= INDENT_MIN else 0.0
    if WORD.fullmatch(token):
        letters = len(token.strip().lstrip("._/-"))
        return None, min(CAP, max(0.0, SLOPE * (letters - LETTERS_AT_ZERO)))
    if CJK.fullmatch(token.strip()):
        return None, min(CAP, max(0.0, CJK_SLOPE * (len(token.strip()) - CJK_AT_ZERO)))
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 6141, as a readable rule set.

It is a sparse, mostly silent feature with three concepts it responds to:
  * POSITIVE on the text "xe" of a hex escape such as \\xe2\\x80\\x9c (escaped
    UTF-8 bytes of a curly quote, or any multi-byte character written out in
    bytes), and more weakly on the "\\xe" token.
  * NEGATIVE on an escaped dollar sign "\\$" (Perl/PHP sigil or LaTeX currency),
    strongest on " \\$" with a space before it.
  * Mildly NEGATIVE on math-function names (lim, sin, exp, inf, det, dim, ...)
    and on a few LaTeX operators written as backslash pairs (*\\, (\\, _\\, ...).
  * Mildly NEGATIVE on punctuation that opens a document (after <|endoftext|>).
Everything else predicts 0. Values are the average activation of each group in
the training data. This explains only a small share of the variance: most of the
component's activation lives in a long tail of individual tokens.
"""
READS = ()

HEX_ESCAPE_LEAD = {"xe": 2.2, "\\xe": 0.6}
ESCAPED_DOLLAR = {" \\$": -1.6, "\\$": -0.6, "(\\$": -0.7, "$_": -0.5}
MATH_FUNCTION = {"lim", "sin", "cos", "exp", "det", "dim", "deg", "inf", "sup", "ln"}
LATEX_OPERATOR_PAIR = {"*\\", "(\\", "=\\", "+\\", "|\\", "_\\", "\\_"}
DOC_START_PUNCT = -0.17


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if token in HEX_ESCAPE_LEAD:
        return carry, HEX_ESCAPE_LEAD[token]
    if token in ESCAPED_DOLLAR:
        return carry, ESCAPED_DOLLAR[token]
    if token.strip() in MATH_FUNCTION:
        return carry, -0.35
    if token in LATEX_OPERATOR_PAIR:
        return carry, -0.2
    stripped = token.strip()
    if starts_doc and stripped and all(not ch.isalnum() for ch in stripped):
        return carry, DOC_START_PUNCT
    return carry, 0.0
